note.text: Trade can be measured as physical quantities or as monetary values. A total physical tonnage requires compatible units and a specified period and boundary. Adding exports and imports gives a total flow measure when defined that way; subtracting gives a balance instead. Monetary trade value can change with prices even when physical quantities do not. Published volume indices may use constant-price methods rather than raw tonnage.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish physical trade quantity from money value and calculate a comparable total. Builds on: transport flows and network maps. Leads to: regional trade arrangements.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented port-month record, exports weigh {120} tonnes and imports {180} tonnes. Combined handled trade is {120+180} tonnes. This does not measure export earnings, an export-minus-import balance or value added. If prices change while these weights stay fixed, trade money values may change without the physical tonnage changing.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Name the measure, units, area and period before calculating. Add compatible physical quantities for the stated combined flow. Do not add tonnes to CFA francs or assume every published use of volume means a simple total weight.
